memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then his father Isaac said to him, 'Come here, my son, and kiss me.' So he went to him and kissed him. When Isaac caught the smell of his clothes, he blessed him and said, 'Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed. May God give you heaven's dew and earth's richness—an abundance of grain and new wine. May nations serve you and peoples bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed and those who bless you be blessed.'" - Gen 27:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The blessing is finally spoken. Isaac calls for prosperity, leadership, and honour to rest on the son before him — words that echo the great promise once given to Abraham. And though the whole scene is soaked in deceit, God's larger purpose still moves forward: the covenant blessing comes to rest on Jacob, just as God had foretold (Gen 25:23).

This is one of the mysteries of Scripture. God's sovereign plan cannot be defeated by human sin — but that does not mean God approves of the sin used along the way. Jacob and Rebekah did not need to lie for God's word to come true. God would have given Jacob the blessing without a single deception. Their scheming did not advance God's plan; it only added guilt and grief to a promise God intended to give freely.

There is deep comfort here for us: our failures cannot ultimately wreck God's good purposes. And there is a warning too: we should never treat God's sovereignty as an excuse for sin, imagining the end justifies the means.

The greatest blessing of all is not stolen or earned by cleverness. In Christ, God freely blesses us "with every spiritual blessing" (Eph 1:3). We need not grasp; we need only receive.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God's good purposes cannot be wrecked by my failures?
2. Am I ever tempted to think a good end justifies wrong means?
3. Have I received the free blessing God offers in Christ, rather than grasping for it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, thank You that Your purposes stand even through our failures. Keep me from excusing sin, and help me to receive Your blessing in Christ with open hands. Amen.
